extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly / general educated public interested in science and natural history
extracted.subtask_description: A miscellany of short popular-science reports and notes (late-19th-century) covering public-health advice, natural-history observations, materials science experiments, travel reports, and technical specifications. Each item is a brief report or recommendation rather than a formal research paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching color-names and education of the color-sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Urge the teaching of color-names and the education of the color-sense in public schools; teaching has been partly introduced into primary schools but without any system; Europe (Germany) has begun systematic instruction in the lowest schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Jeffries' inquiries show lack of knowledge of color-names among adults and schoolboys; systematic teaching from earliest grades is recommended and, if effective, might reduce incidence of color-naming deficiencies in future generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tropical residence rule: diet, exercise, and energy
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule of life for residents in the tropics should be based on 'diet, exercise, and energy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance includes adopting a lighter diet (reducing richness and quantity of food rather than increasing it), maintaining regular judicious exercise at different times of day and year, avoiding excessive use of spirits, guarding against carelessness of exposure, preserving mental activity and social variety to prevent apathy and cognitive decline, and generally cultivating bodily robustness to withstand climatic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary precautions for Europeans in tropical countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Europeans going to tropical countries must obey the appropriate dietary laws of the climate and country and avoid indulgence in rich viands, high seasonings, and wines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mistakes include increasing quantity and richness of food under the impression that climate-induced exhaustion requires more food; instead a lighter varied diet is required, as excessive richness burdens the stomach and leads to disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary siting and measures to prevent malaria
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid building or allowing towns to grow near marshes or lagoons; apply sanitary science to improve unhealthy coastal towns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natives' protective measures (planting groves between swamps and villages, burning bush to crust soil) are effectual means of warding off malaria; failure to adopt such measures in colonial possessions contributes to unhealthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acclimatization and remedies for mountain (altitude) sickness
rubrics_metrics.description: Acclimatize gradually by spending days at increasing altitudes; symptoms may abate after several days and on descent they may disappear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Whymper's account: spent multiple nights at intermediate heights (e.g., 13,400 ft, ten nights at 16,500 ft, six at 17,300 ft) and observed symptoms ease; chlorate of potash afforded relief; prior long residence at 9,000–10,000 ft conferred partial immunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize physical structure when evaluating dyeing behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical structure of substances submitted to dyeing (capillarity, minute central canals) may be of much more importance than their chemical composition in determining dye uptake and fixation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M. Engel's experiments: siliceous sands composed of tubular diatom carapaces behaved like cotton or wool in presence of certain dyes; microscopic examination of fiber structure (central canals, capillarity) can predict dyeing behavior; examples include sands dyed with alizarine rose, indigo, logwood and sands behaving like wool with aniline-derived dyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public funding criterion for scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: Public money should not be granted for scientific research unless it appears that results useful to the public will be obtained or the work would not be undertaken by private individuals or bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolutions voiced disapproval of founding a physical observatory at national expense and recommended discontinuing grants (e.g., Government grant to Committee on Solar Physics) unless justified; also called for publication of full accounts of government scientific expenditures and clear definitions of the nature of the work to be undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic features indicating frost-formed (frost-drift) earth-beds
rubrics_metrics.description: Superficial earth coverings that are unstratified, interspersed with pebbles and coarser stones (heavier fragments tending to the bottom), and lacking indications of water stratification point to frost action rather than water deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professor Kerr argues frost of the glacial period could penetrate and decompose rock in situ producing 'frost-drift' with mineral veins breaking up and fragments scattered—examples from Market Street (Philadelphia) and a mica-mine in North Carolina; implies assessing bedding lines, presence/absence of water stratification, and relationships to mineral veins when interpreting deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ritual procedure for capturing and burying the soul of the drowned (Abchasian rite)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a drowned person's body is not found, friends perform a ritual to capture the soul: prepare a goat-skin bag, stretch its mouth open over a hoop facing the river, stretch two cords across the river as a bridge for the soul, set food and drink around the skin, sing with instruments to attract the soul, close and carry the inflated bag to a prepared grave and 'squeeze' the soul into the grave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rite is believed equivalent in value to burial of the body and the grave is treated with the same honor as if the body were interred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance and remediation of alkali accumulation from irrigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary surface irrigation on alkaline lands concentrates alkali at the surface; remedy by underdraining to lower the water-table and favor washing out salts during rainy seasons so they fail to reach and accumulate at the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional measures: cultivate deep-rooted crops, use gypsum, employ sub-irrigation, and periodically leach salts by long continued flooding combined with underdrainage. Observation from California (Kern and Tulare lakes) indicates many river-waters will, under continued irrigation without underdrainage, eventually cause injurious soluble salt accumulation in soils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design specification for the new Eddystone Lighthouse light
rubrics_metrics.description: The light will be oscillating: a powerful white, double-flashing half-minute light showing two successive flashes of about 2.5 seconds' duration divided by an eclipse of about 4 seconds, the second flash followed by an eclipse of about 21 seconds; visible all around the horizon for 17.5 miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tower built of uniform granite and double the height of the old one; a subsidiary white light will be mounted in an upper room to cover the Hand Deeps and adjusted to be seen only within the danger area to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and purification steps for papaine (vegetable digestive agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain milky juice by incising epidermis of Carica papaya; bottle juice either pure or mixed with 10–12% alcohol to prevent fermentation; alcohol precipitates crude papaine which is washed in alcohol and ether, redissolved in water, re-precipitated, and purified by dialysis; refining with sub-acetate of lead yields characteristic properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of the juice's physical characteristics (white, slightly bitter, styptic, acid reaction, high in albumen) and lab procedures (alcohol/ether washing, dialysis) are provided; purified papaine is described as an albuminoid substance very soluble in water.
